title: Erdős #740: The Bipartite (r = ∞) Case Fails, with Real Chromatic Numbers
description: The existing erdos-740 formalization rests on a placeholder chromatic number (chromaticNumber V G := Cardinal.mk V), so its open 'no_infinite_bipartite' sorry is not a statement about the real invariant. This entry replaces that fragment with an honest, fully proved result using Mathlib's genuine SimpleGraph.chromaticNumber (ℕ∞-valued) and SimpleGraph.IsBipartite (= Colorable 2). The limiting r = ∞ case of Erdős #740 asks for a bipartite (odd-cycle-free) subgraph of full chromatic number; we prove this case FAILS — a bipartite graph has χ ≤ 2, so when χ(G) > 2 no induced bipartite subgraph realizes χ(G) — and give explicit witnesses (the triangle K₃ and every Kₙ, n ≥ 3).

overview.historicalContext:
Erdős Problem #740 (Erdős–Hajnal) asks: if a graph `G` has chromatic number an infinite cardinal `𝔪`, and `r ≥ 1`, must `G` contain a subgraph of chromatic number `𝔪` containing no odd cycle of length `≤ r`? Rödl (1982) proved the countable case `𝔪 = ℵ₀`, `r = 3`; the general problem is open and was listed by Erdős among problems he 'would most like to see solved'.

The parameter `r` interpolates between two extremes. At `r = 3` one forbids triangles; as `r → ∞` one forbids odd cycles of every length, which is exactly the condition that the subgraph be **bipartite**. The bipartite extreme behaves very differently from the finite-`r` regime: a bipartite graph is `2`-colourable, so it can never have chromatic number exceeding `2`. Consequently the `r = ∞` version of #740 is *false* for any graph of chromatic number `> 2` — there is simply no bipartite subgraph of large chromatic number to be found.

The existing gallery file `Erdos740Problem.lean` set up this dichotomy but defined `chromaticNumber V G := Cardinal.mk V` as an explicit placeholder, so its `no_infinite_bipartite` statement (left as a `sorry`) was not about the real chromatic number. This entry redoes the bipartite case honestly, on top of Mathlib's genuine `SimpleGraph.chromaticNumber` and `SimpleGraph.IsBipartite`.
overview.problemStatement: Using the real chromatic number, prove the bipartite (r = ∞) case of Erdős #740: a bipartite graph has chromatic number at most 2, so if χ(G) > 2 there is no induced bipartite subgraph H of G with χ(H) = χ(G). Provide explicit non-vacuous witnesses (K₃, and Kₙ for n ≥ 3).
overview.proofStrategy: Three ingredients, all from Mathlib's colouring theory. (1) Monotonicity: the inclusion G.induce s ↪g G is a graph homomorphism, so chromaticNumber_mono_of_hom gives χ(G.induce s) ≤ χ(G). (2) Bipartite bound: IsBipartite unfolds to Colorable 2, and Colorable.chromaticNumber_le gives χ ≤ 2. (3) Contradiction: if an induced bipartite subgraph had χ equal to χ(G), then χ(G) ≤ 2, contradicting χ(G) > 2. For witnesses, chromaticNumber_top gives χ(Kₙ) = |Fin n| = n, and 2 < n for n ≥ 3.
keyInsights: The r = ∞ extreme of Erdős #740 is the bipartite case: 'no odd cycle of any length' is exactly 'bipartite' is exactly '2-colourable'.
Bipartite graphs are a hard ceiling: χ ≤ 2 always. So the only obstruction needed to refute the bipartite version of #740 is the elementary bound χ(bipartite) ≤ 2.
Induced subgraphs never raise the chromatic number, since the inclusion is a homomorphism — a clean instance of the general principle χ is monotone under homomorphisms.
The failure is non-vacuous and concrete: the triangle already has χ = 3 > 2, and every complete graph Kₙ with n ≥ 3 witnesses it.

Honesty matters: the parent file's placeholder chromaticNumber := Cardinal.mk V makes its statements meaningless; switching to Mathlib's real invariant turns the intended claim into a genuine theorem.

conclusion.summary: A fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide) treatment, in 108 lines with 8 theorems, of the bipartite (r = ∞) case of Erdős #740, using Mathlib's genuine chromatic number. The core result: a graph with χ > 2 has no induced bipartite subgraph realizing its chromatic number, because bipartite graphs have χ ≤ 2. Explicit witnesses (K₃ and every Kₙ, n ≥ 3) make the failure concrete.
conclusion.implications: This replaces the placeholder-based open 'no_infinite_bipartite' fragment of the parent erdos-740 entry with an honest, machine-checked statement about the real invariant. It pins down the boundary behaviour of Erdős #740: the problem is genuinely about FINITE r (where Rödl's r = 3, 𝔪 = ℵ₀ result lives and the general case is open); the r = ∞ (bipartite) extreme is settled in the negative by the elementary χ(bipartite) ≤ 2 bound. The induced-subgraph monotonicity lemma is a reusable building block for further chromatic-number formalizations.
openQuestions: Formalize Rödl's theorem (𝔪 = ℵ₀, r = 3): a graph of chromatic number ℵ₀ contains a triangle-free subgraph of chromatic number ℵ₀ — the genuine positive result of #740.
Formalize the finite analogue with real chromatic numbers: does there exist f_r(k) such that χ(G) ≥ f_r(k) forces a subgraph with χ ≥ k and no odd cycle of length ≤ r?
